entries.sense_en: stripped bare; with everything that covered or decorated it taken away

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word; take a covering or layer off something.
synonyms.example: strip the paint off the door

synonyms.nuance: Usually an adjective or to expose on purpose; less about removing something that was there.
Formal; take away rank, power or possessions, not physical covering.

entries.modern: "denuded of the light" → "stripped of the light"

entries.sense_en: table linen: tablecloths and napkins

synonyms.nuance: The ordinary modern phrase for the same thing.
One single cloth; napery is the whole set, and old or formal.
Broader: includes bed sheets and towels as well as table cloths.

entries.sense_en: deliberately confusing, making someone believe something puzzling or false

synonyms.nuance: Hard to understand; does not suggest anyone is doing it on purpose.
Stronger: so confusing that you cannot find any explanation.
Gives a wrong idea, often unintentionally; focuses on the false impression.

entries.modern: "He was mystifying!" → "He was pulling my leg!"
entries.tip_ko: 현대 영어의 mystifying은 보통 '이해하기 힘든'이지만, 여기서는 '일부러 사람을 속여 어리둥절하게 하는'이라는 옛 뜻입니다.

entries.sense_en: lack of effort or care in doing one's duty

synonyms.nuance: A general character flaw; slackness is failing to work hard enough at a particular job.
Failing to take proper care, often with serious results; more formal and legal.
Formal; rules or standards not enforced strictly enough.

entries.sense_en: not willing to talk about his feelings or private matters
entries.sense_ko: 자기 속내를 잘 털어놓지 않는, 과묵한

synonyms.nuance: Similar, but describes a cool, private manner in general, not just about one subject.
Nervous with people; a reticent person may be confident but simply chooses to say little.
Informal; deliberately refusing to give information.

entries.tip_ko: 'reluctant(내키지 않는)'와 혼동하지 마세요. reticent는 말을 아끼는 것입니다.

entries.sense_en: an accusation that someone has done something bad or is at fault

synonyms.nuance: Everyday and direct; imputation is formal and often hints at fault without proof.
Suggests something bad indirectly, without saying it openly.
A claim, usually about a crime, not yet proved; common in news.

entries.sense_en: ghostly figures that suddenly appear

synonyms.nuance: Common word for the spirit of a dead person.
More literary; something seen that is unreal or hard to grasp.
Literary; a frightening ghost, or a threatening idea.

entries.sense_en: kept returning to his mind and would not leave him alone

synonyms.nuance: Fill the mind so completely you think of nothing else; less about the past or ghosts.
Stronger: cause constant pain or suffering.
Trouble again and again over time, like a disease or problem.

entries.match: takes the light out of things
entries.headword: take the light out of things
entries.sense_en: makes everything else seem dull and joyless
entries.sense_ko: 모든 것에서 빛과 재미를 앗아 가다

synonyms.nuance: Reduce enthusiasm or spirits a little.
Stronger and more literal; slowly empties out happiness.
synonyms.example: it drained the joy from her work

synonyms.nuance: Spoil a happy event or time with something sad or worrying.
synonyms.example: the news cast a shadow over the party

entries.sense_en: so strong that it can never be satisfied

synonyms.nuance: Literary; a desire that cannot be put out, like thirst or fire.
Plain word about length or amount; says nothing about wanting.
Negative: wanting too much; insatiable can be neutral or even admiring.

entries.sense_en: make an impression on society, be noticed and admired
entries.sense_ko: 세상에서 두각을 나타내다, 눈에 띄는 인물이 되다

synonyms.nuance: Become famous or respected through achievement.
synonyms.example: she made a name for herself in law

synonyms.nuance: Simply be noticeable; not necessarily successful.
synonyms.example: he stands out in a crowd

synonyms.nuance: Informal; get sudden, strong attention.

entries.tip_ko: 'cut a fine/poor figure'처럼 형용사를 붙여 '~한 모습을 보이다'로도 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: not care at all

synonyms.nuance: Neutral, modern everyday version.
Much ruder and stronger.
Common, emphatic; total lack of interest.

entries.modern: "doesn't care a rap" → "doesn't care at all"

entries.sense_en: never dying; lasting forever

synonyms.nuance: Without beginning or end in time; often about feelings or truths.
Continuing forever from now on; warmer, less formal.
Literary; used of feelings that never fade.

entries.sense_en: developing mental abilities much earlier than most children

synonyms.nuance: Has a natural talent; says nothing about being early.
Neutral; ahead of others for their age.
Behaves like an adult; precocious stresses skills arriving unusually early.

entries.sense_en: in a moment, very quickly

synonyms.nuance: Very common; suggests something sudden and bright or quick.
Everyday; emphasises how little time was needed.
Neutral, slightly more formal.
synonyms.example: in an instant, he was gone

entries.sense_en: suddenly and straight, without stopping to think

synonyms.nuance: Plain direction word, no sense of suddenness.
Rushing forward recklessly, without looking.
Informal; exactly, directly, often with a sound or impact.

entries.sense_en: made one feel lively, cheerful and full of energy
entries.sense_ko: 기분을 들뜨게 하다, 활력이 넘치게 하다

synonyms.nuance: Milder: lift someone's spirits a little.
Sharp, short excitement, often with a little fear.
Give physical or mental energy, like fresh air or a cold shower.

entries.sense_en: seeming to glow softly with light

synonyms.nuance: Everyday; gives off a steady warm light.
Shines brightly, often used of happy faces.
Plain word for lots of light; luminous suggests a gentle inner glow.

entries.sense_en: was quiet and lost in thought before continuing

synonyms.nuance: Think carefully about a specific question or decision.
Let the mind drift pleasantly, not seriously.
Think for a long time about something sad or angry.

entries.sense_en: touched softly and lovingly

synonyms.nuance: Move the hand gently along, e.g. a pet; less romantic.
Quick, light taps, not a continuous movement.
Touch lovingly but can sound improper with people.

entries.sense_en: a covered walkway with a row of columns along it

synonyms.nuance: A row of arches, not flat-topped columns; often with shops.
A columned porch at the entrance of a building.
A covered walk around a courtyard, typically in a monastery.

entries.sense_en: small, long-tailed, brightly coloured parrots

synonyms.nuance: The modern spelling of the same word.
General word; usually bigger and able to copy speech.
Informal; the small pet parakeet.

entries.sense_en: dark in colour and serious or gloomy in manner

synonyms.nuance: Serious and dignified, especially at formal or sad events; not necessarily gloomy.
More openly sad, depressed or dark.
Serious and worrying; a grave look or matter.

entries.sense_en: unwilling; not wanting to let him go

synonyms.nuance: The everyday word; a little weaker and more common.
Flatly not ready to do it; less about feelings.
Formal; strongly disliking, usually with 'to'.

entries.tip_ko: 동사 loathe(/loʊð/, 몹시 싫어하다)와 발음·철자가 달라요.

entries.sense_en: paid attention to

synonyms.nuance: Plain word; hearing does not always mean acting on it.
Everyday and neutral.
Become aware of and react to something.

entries.modern: "heeded them not at all" → "didn't pay any attention to them"

entries.sense_en: kind and wishing to help others

synonyms.nuance: Warm and gentle in manner; the everyday word.
Giving help or money to the needy, or judging others gently.
Willing to give freely, especially money or time.

entries.sense_en: poking with the end of something

synonyms.nuance: Push quickly with a finger or stick; the most common word.
Push gently, usually with the elbow, to get attention.
A sharper, harder, faster poke.

entries.sense_en: felt he had to, insisted on, in an irritating way

synonyms.nuance: Demand or refuse to do otherwise; modern verb.
Sense a duty; less annoyed tone.
Plain necessity, with no note of annoyance.

entries.modern: "he must needs bring in a policeman" → "he had to go and bring in a policeman"

entries.sense_en: a hard beating as punishment

synonyms.nuance: General word for hitting someone repeatedly.
Lighter: slaps on the bottom, only for young children.
Hits with a whip or cane; often formal punishment.

entries.tip_ko: 'thr-'의 th는 /θ/로 혀끝을 이 사이에 두고 발음합니다.

entries.sense_en: an unlucky event or small accident

synonyms.nuance: A small accident with little harm.
Bad luck in general, sometimes serious.
synonyms.example: the misfortune of losing his job

synonyms.nuance: Old-fashioned; a piece of bad luck.

entries.sense_en: caught up in a confusing maze of streets

synonyms.nuance: Simple adjective for twisted threads or hair.
Trapped by something, without the twisting idea.
Mixed up in a situation, often complicated.

entries.sense_en: a street closed at one end, with no way through

synonyms.nuance: Everyday phrase; also used for hopeless situations.
A narrow alley closed at one end; often figurative for a career with no future.
British name for a short residential street with one end closed.

entries.tip_ko: 프랑스어에서 온 말이지만 미국 영어에서는 '컬 더 색'처럼 읽습니다.

entries.sense_en: shabby, untidy and slightly dirty

synonyms.nuance: Worn out and poorly kept.
Informal; untidy, especially of people or clothes.
Run-down and slightly disreputable.

entries.sense_en: struck his mind suddenly and forcefully (he realised)

synonyms.nuance: Plain word; here it means a sudden idea 'hit' him.
A slow, gradual realisation, unlike a sudden blow.
Sudden thought that comes into the mind.

entries.sense_en: the habit of arriving on time

synonyms.nuance: Acting quickly and without delay, not only being on time.
Happening at just the right time; about events or actions.
Broader: doing what you say you will.

entries.sense_en: with the mind pulled elsewhere so that one cannot concentrate (here from excited daydreaming, not distress)
entries.sense_ko: 정신이 딴 데 팔린, 마음이 들떠 산만한

synonyms.nuance: The modern word for this older sense: mind elsewhere, unable to focus.
Not noticing what one is doing because of thinking of other things; often a habit.
Unhappy or worried; the feeling modern distraught suggests, which is not meant here.

entries.tip_ko: 현대 영어의 distraught는 보통 '몹시 괴로워 제정신이 아닌'이지만, 여기서는 '정신이 딴 데 팔린'이라는 옛 뜻입니다.

entries.sense_en: demanding great effort and energy

synonyms.nuance: Needing a lot of skill, time or attention; not necessarily physical.
Long and tiring, like a difficult journey; more formal.
Full of energy; describes the way someone acts.

entries.sense_en: extra work given to a schoolboy as punishment

synonyms.nuance: General word for any penalty.
Being kept at school after hours as a punishment.
British school: sentences copied out many times as a punishment.

entries.tip_ko: 현대 영어에서 imposition은 보통 '부담이 되는 부탁'을 뜻합니다.

entries.sense_en: having a thin, sharp, sly face like a ferret

synonyms.nuance: Similar, and stronger: looks sly and untrustworthy.
Neutral; just thin and pointed in the face.
Looks dishonest, especially in the eyes.

entries.sense_en: told a secret carelessly

synonyms.nuance: Say something suddenly without thinking.
Informal; reveal a secret, often 'spill the beans'.
Talk about other people's private lives; usually not one secret.

entries.sense_en: a hidden feeling that pulls in the opposite direction

synonyms.nuance: Hidden feeling or trend beneath the surface; broader and more common.
Any flow of water or air; not hidden.
Plain word for a force drawing you.

entries.sense_en: done without any good reason and without care for the harm

synonyms.nuance: Has no purpose or meaning; less about cruelty.
Unnecessary and unjustified, especially of violence or insults.
Intended to harm; wanton may simply be careless.

entries.sense_en: crying noisily, like a child

synonyms.nuance: Cry with short, sharp breaths; may be quiet and dignified.
Weak, small, quiet crying.
Cry loudly, like a baby.

entries.tip_ko: 철자가 같은 명사 blubber는 '고래 지방'이라는 뜻입니다.

entries.sense_en: letting the mind wander instead of paying attention

synonyms.nuance: Common word; pleasant thoughts, not always a fault.
Same as the headword, written as one word; a little old-fashioned.
A habit of not noticing what one is doing.

entries.sense_en: hard, dull, repeated work, especially study

synonyms.nuance: Boring, tiring work with no reward; more negative and literary.
Common fuller phrase for tiresome routine work.
Just a regular pattern; not necessarily unpleasant.

entries.sense_en: a two-wheeled horse-drawn cab for hire
entries.sense_ko: (19세기의) 두 바퀴 영업용 마차, 핸섬 캡

synonyms.nuance: General: a hired vehicle, then horse-drawn, now a taxi.
Any horse-drawn passenger vehicle, often private.
Modern motor version of the hired cab.

entries.sense_en: without planning, taking a chance

synonyms.nuance: By chance, without any pattern or choice.
Hoping something might work though unlikely.
Suddenly, following a feeling.

entries.sense_en: a dull film that spoils the shine of metal, here a loss of brightness in life
entries.sense_ko: (금속 표면의) 변색; 여기서는 삶의 빛이 바램

synonyms.nuance: A mark that stays on a surface, often dirty.
Plain lack of shine or interest.
Reddish damage to iron and steel only; tarnish is on silver, brass, etc.

entries.sense_en: needing long, hard, tiring effort

synonyms.nuance: Needing much slow effort; more formal and neutral.
Difficult and tiring over a long time.
Everyday word for making you feel tired.

entries.sense_en: having a pale, bluish-grey colour, like a bruise

synonyms.nuance: Unhealthily pale, no blue tone.
Grey-white, from shock or illness.
The common modern meaning of livid: very angry.

entries.tip_ko: 요즘은 '몹시 화난'이라는 뜻으로 더 자주 쓰이지만, 여기서는 색깔을 뜻합니다.

entries.sense_en: not matched with an opposing member who agreed to skip the vote, so free to be called in
entries.sense_ko: (의회에서) 상대편 의원과 불참 협정을 맺지 않은

synonyms.nuance: General: without a partner or equal.
Available to be summoned when needed.
Not linked to anyone or anything.

entries.tip_ko: 영국 의회 용어: 'pairing'은 반대 당 의원끼리 서로 불참하기로 약속하는 제도입니다.

entries.sense_en: walked slowly and easily, without hurry

synonyms.nuance: Walk for pleasure; slightly more neutral.
Walk at a slow, relaxed pace; very close to saunter, a little less carefree.
Walk without a fixed direction.

entries.sense_en: cheap, showy and of poor quality

synonyms.nuance: Too bright and flashy in colour.
Informal; in poor taste.
Badly made; about quality not looks.

entries.sense_en: tiresome and annoying, especially because it goes on

synonyms.nuance: Common word, can be brief.
Boring and too long.
Wearing on the patience over time.

entries.sense_en: so strong that nothing can calm or satisfy it
entries.sense_ko: 달랠 수 없는, 가라앉힐 수 없는

synonyms.nuance: Same meaning, more common form.
Cannot be calmed, usually anger or an enemy; harder, more hostile.
Too sad to be comforted.

entries.sense_en: foremen who supervise a gang of workmen

synonyms.nuance: General word for a worker in charge of others.
Modern, formal; any position of oversight.
Old-fashioned; someone who watches workers.

entries.sense_en: a temporary wooden fence around a building site

synonyms.nuance: General barrier; not just around building work.
Blocks the way to stop people passing.
In British English hoarding also means an advertising board; a billboard is only that.

entries.tip_ko: hoarding은 보통 '사재기, 비축'(동사 hoard)이라는 뜻으로 더 많이 쓰입니다. 이 '가림 울타리' 뜻은 영국 영어입니다.
